maya: heads-up — after last night's kernel-selection rollout we're seeing intermittent GPU OOMs during prefix cache warmup for chat_v2. spike at ~02:17 UTC on gpu-pool-3
liam: ugh, saw that alert. OOMs correlate with a ~15s latency tail and sudden 4x token compute. logs show cache insert storms
anika: can you paste the log snippet? also what cache config? per-model TTL changed in that rollout?
maya: snippet: ```
2026-03-12T02:17:09Z ERROR serve: oom allocating 1.2GB for kv-cache shard
model=chat_v2 variant=q8h epoch=20260312-ker-sel
active_prefixes=21874 cache_hits=0 cache_inserts=21790
```
maya: config: prefix_cache.enabled=true, ttl_seconds=3600 -> was 86400 previously, per_model_cache_limit_pct=30
liam: wait we lowered TTL to 1h intentionally to reduce stale growth. but that many inserts suggests churn + key normalization mismatch
tom: perf-ops: profiling dump shows heavy fragmentation on GPU memory after rapid insert/evict cycles. sample from nvprof: ```
GPU mem free before insert: 12.1GB
after 120s of warmup: 0.2GB, fragmentation 35%
```
anika: possible cause: cache keys include session id in some paths? meaning near-unique keys -> low hit rate and huge insert churn
maya: confirmed — observed keys like: "user_123:turn_4:system_prompt_hash:..."; keying should be normalized to prefix_hash + model + role_sequence
liam: hit-rate numbers from last 6h: overall hit_rate=6.3%, median prefix_len=42 tokens, insert_rate=5.2k/s during the 02:00-02:20 window
perf-ops: we also saw batching heuristic change in rollout: small batch aggregation lowered max_batch_delay from 10ms to 2ms which increased effective per-request overhead and killed batching efficiency during warmup
tom: that aligns — more small batches -> more KV loads/inserts concurrently -> more fragmentation and more allocator pressure
maya: hypothesis: combo of shorter TTL + poor keying + reduced batching = insert storm -> allocator churn -> OOMs on peak
anika: mitigation ideas: 1) revert TTL to 24h 2) normalize keys server-side to drop session-specific noise 3) reintroduce batching headroom (max_batch_delay=8ms) 4) add per-model cache admission cap
liam: quick patch: disable the TTL change and set per_model_cache_limit_pct=20, bump batch_delay to 8ms. rolling this now to prod canary
perf-ops: also recommend enabling demotion-to-CPU for entries older than X inserts to reduce GPU pressure (experimental but low-risk)
maya: rolling config via deploy-bot: ```
deploy-bot: rolling config update to gateway-config: prefix_cache.ttl_seconds=86400, prefix_cache.per_model_limit_pct=20, runtime.max_batch_delay_ms=8
```
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-20260312-047 — "prefix-cache warmup OOMs (chat_v2)" assigned to eng-runtime oncall
anika: after the partial rollback to TTL 24h and batch_delay=8ms we saw insert_rate drop ~70% in the canary pool and hit_rate improved to 18% within 10 minutes
liam: nice. but still see fragmentation in long-running processes. need background compaction / allocator tuning for CUDA pool
tom: follow-up tasks I propose: 
- add key-normalization middleware in runtime to canonicalize prefixes
- add cache admission policy: min_hit_thresh and per-prefix cap
- implement async prewarm that feeds top-k prefixes at cold start (staggered across nodes)
- GPU allocator compaction or periodic memdefrag in idle windows
perf-ops: profiling data to attach: p99 mem frag and per-call alloc traces. i'll upload artifact to the runbook
maya: note for rollouts: add perf regression gate that checks insert_rate and cache_hit_rate on canary for 30m before full rollout
anika: also add unit test for key derivation to prevent accidental inclusion of session-specific fields in keying
liam: can someone own a short postmortem with timeline + metric diffs? i'll draft initial bullets, assign to maya to fill details
maya: taking it. will include commands used to snapshot counts: ```
# count active prefixes
redis-cli -h cache-prod HGET chat_v2 stats:active_prefixes
# sample hit rate
curl -s http://metrics:9090/query?query=prefix_cache_hit_ratio
```
maya: thanks everyone. no user-facing impact reported, but this was close. learned: TTL reductions + keying bugs are a dangerous combo when batching changes land simultaneously :thumbsup:
